questions.q: A scene starts with two lovers trusting each other and ends with them still trusting each other, after ten minutes of talk. McKee would call it…
questions.explain: If the value at stake doesn't change charge, nothing has happened.

choices: The space between expectation and result when a character acts
The distance between author and narrator
The difference between story and plot
questions.explain: The world reacts differently than the character expects, forcing a riskier action.

questions.q: Put McKee's five parts in order:
choices: Crisis, inciting incident, complications, climax, resolution
Inciting incident, progressive complications, crisis, climax, resolution
Inciting incident, crisis, complications, resolution, climax
Complications, inciting incident, climax, crisis, resolution
questions.explain: The crisis is the dilemma; the climax is the action that answers it.

questions.q: In McKee's terms, the crisis is…
choices: A true dilemma that forces a choice
The low point after the midpoint
questions.explain: A choice between irreconcilable goods or the lesser of two evils, where character is revealed.

questions.q: A clever, charming hero turns out to be capable of cruelty under pressure. McKee calls this the contrast between…
questions.explain: True character is revealed by choices made under pressure, and great stories contrast it with the surface.

questions.q: Which design has a passive protagonist, inner conflict and an open ending?
questions.explain: Miniplot (minimalism) sits at one corner of McKee's story triangle.

questions.q: How does McKee decide how many acts a story has?
questions.explain: Acts are defined by act climaxes, major reversals, not a template.

ideas: Every scene must turn a value from positive to negative, or the reverse; otherwise it's a non-event.
Progress comes from the gap between what a character expects their action to do and what the world actually does.
Story design ranges across a triangle: classical archplot, minimalist miniplot and anti-structural antiplot.
True character is revealed in the choices a person makes under pressure.
